memory.guide.label: When cleaning helps
memory.guide.title: When cleaning helps, and when it does not
memory.guide.helps.body: right after a game, an editor or an AI model that held a lot of memory has closed and something else needs a large amount at once, or when you want a clean starting point to measure from.
memory.guide.doesNot.body: just because the standby number is large. Standby memory is a cache: Windows gives it back by itself the moment a program asks for memory, so it is not wasted. Emptying it makes the next things you open load from disk, which is slower. Cleaning also does not speed up a PC that has too little memory for what it runs, and it does not fix a program that keeps growing.

apps.footnote: Volt never lists itself, and it only starts the uninstaller an app registered. Removals are listed on the Undo page, which cannot reverse them.
tidy.where.label: Folders to look in
tidy.readonly: Looking only. The Windows, Program Files and ProgramData folders, links and system files are left out. Nothing changes until you move items yourself.
tidy.empty.title: Find duplicates and clutter
tidy.empty.description: Add the folders to look in and Volt lists duplicate files, empty folders and shortcuts that point nowhere. You choose what moves to the Recycle Bin.
tidy.stage.comparing: Comparing files of the same size... {done} of {total} done, {size} read.
tidy.note.cloud: {count} cloud-only files were not downloaded or compared.
tidy.note.hardLinks: {count} extra names of the same file (hard links) are not counted as duplicates.
tidy.note.shortcuts: {count} shortcuts could not be judged and are not listed.
tidy.note.truncated: The scan reached its size limit, so part of the folders was not looked at.
tidy.dup.title: Duplicate files
tidy.dup.hint: Files of {size} or more with exactly the same content, found by size and then by content, not by name. Pick the copy to keep and the others are marked; you can change the marks. At least one copy of every group always stays. Two names of one file (hard links) are not duplicates.
tidy.dup.hardLinks: Other names of this file (hard links): {count}, not counted.
tidy.dup.lastCopy: The last copy that is not marked stays.
tidy.dup.keepAria: Keep {name} and mark the other copies
tidy.dup.selection.some: {selection} marked. They will be moved to the Recycle Bin, not deleted.
tidy.folders.title: Empty folders
tidy.folders.hint: A folder counts as empty when nothing is in it, or only other empty folders. A folder with any file in it (hidden, read-only or zero bytes too), a link, a folder that cannot be read, a system folder and the folders you chose are never listed.
tidy.shortcuts.title: Shortcuts with a missing target
tidy.shortcuts.hint: A shortcut is listed when the file or folder it points to is gone while its drive is connected. A shortcut to a drive or share that is not connected, to a removable, optical or network drive, or to something that is not a path (an app, a Control Panel item) is never listed.
tidy.shortcuts.none: No shortcuts with a missing target were found.
tidy.row.openFailed: The folder could not be opened. {error}
tidy.selection.some: {selection} selected. They will be moved to the Recycle Bin, not deleted.
tidy.confirm.title: Move these to the Recycle Bin?
tidy.confirm.description: {selection} will be moved to the Recycle Bin. Nothing is deleted for good, and files keep using disk space until you empty the Recycle Bin. You can restore them from there.
tidy.confirm.keeps: Each group keeps at least one copy, and a copy that stays is checked again just before.
tidy.result.label: Move result
tidy.result.title: Moved to the Recycle Bin
tidy.result.moved: Moved {items} to the Recycle Bin ({size}). No disk space is freed until the Recycle Bin is emptied.
tidy.result.historyIncomplete: The activity history could not be written, so this move is missing from it.
